title: Oil Prices Hold Near Three-Month Lows Despite Hormuz Mine Claims | OilPrice.com

Crude oil prices remained subdued in early trading on Tuesday, with Brent trading below $90 per barrel despite Iranian claims that three oil tankers had struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $88.67 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $79.59 per barrel, both near the lowest in three months, after October highs of over $100 per barrel for both benchmarks.

“Brent has largely lost any upward impetus in recent days as supply conditions remain benign despite the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz, and the market weighs the possibility of a future supply glut against persistent Middle East tensions and shipping disruptions,” Reuters quoted DBS Bank’s head of energy research, Suvro Sarkar, as saying.

“However, risk of prices going up again cannot be ruled out as nothing has moved in US-Iran talks and both parties could move at some point to test the other's resolve in blockading the strait,” Sarkar added.

Meanwhile, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed three tankers had hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz after they violated the country’s new rules for crossing the waterway. The fact that oil traders dismissed the incidents suggests that reports about oversupply have a stronger effect on trading decisions than tanker traffic disruption in the Persian Gulf.

Even a recent interview of President Trump with Fox News, in which he did not rule out a resumption of hostilities, failed to add fuel to oil prices. “They talk all the time, all they do is talk, but it’s all BS,” President Trump told Fox News correspondents. “They’re more aggressive now than before the election,” the U.S. President said, adding that the Iranian officials are like “professional tap dancers.” He also suggested the U.S. could restart attacks on Iranian targets after the end of the year.
